Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Q3 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Davies, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Janet Davies, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to StellarTech’s earnings call. Joining me today are Mark Thompson, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; and David Lee, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations site. Today’s discussion may include forward-looking statements. With that, let me turn the call over to Mark.

Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet, and welcome everyone.

We’re pleased with our performance this quarter. I want to highlight a few areas.

Let's start with operating margin. We are revising our operating margin guidance for the full year to approximately 32.5%. This is a 0.5 percentage point increase from our previous guidance of 32.0% issued last quarter. While it seems like a modest adjustment, this improvement reflects significant underlying operational efficiencies and strategic execution across several key areas. This positive revision is attributable to a confluence of factors. First, we saw stronger-than-anticipated revenue growth, particularly in high-margin segments. Q3 revenue experienced a robust surge, with a 15% increase year-over-year to $2.3 billion. This growth was particularly pronounced within our cloud-based solutions segment, which saw a 22% increase in revenue, contributing significantly to the overall profitability mix. This segment boasts a higher operating margin, approximately 45%, compared to our more mature hardware division, which is around 28%. The increased proportion of revenue from this higher-margin segment directly improves our consolidated operating margin. We initially forecasted a more conservative growth rate in this sector, but accelerated adoption rates due to enhanced security features and seamless integration with existing infrastructure fueled the outperformance. Also, we successfully implemented a range of cost optimization initiatives throughout the year. These initiatives are now yielding tangible results. For example, we successfully renegotiated key supplier contracts, resulting in a 4% reduction in raw material costs in Q3. We invested $15 million into upgrading our supply chain management system, which now provides real-time visibility and predictive analytics to optimize inventory levels and minimize waste. This has resulted in a 10% reduction in warehousing costs and a 7% decrease in transportation expenses. Our investment in robotic process automation (RPA) within our customer service and finance departments has streamlined operations and reduced headcount in these areas. This initiative, which cost $8 million to implement, is projected to save us $12 million annually. We've seen a 20% reduction in processing time for customer inquiries and a 15% improvement in the accuracy of financial reporting. Further, upgrades to our data centers, including the implementation of advanced cooling technologies and renewable energy sourcing, have reduced our energy consumption by 12%, resulting in significant cost savings and contributing to our ESG goals.

Another important aspect is our Q3 diluted EPS, which reached $1.42, exceeding our initial guidance of $1.24 by a significant $0.18, a 14.5% beat. This exceptional performance was driven by a confluence of factors, primarily a substantial expansion in net margin, coupled with robust revenue growth and effective cost management. Revenue saw a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, surpassing our internal target of $2.2 billion. This impressive growth was largely fueled by strong performance in our cloud-based services segment, which experienced a 22% surge, contributing $850 million to total revenue. Geographically, North America continued to be our strongest market, accounting for 55% of total revenue, but we witnessed particularly encouraging growth in the Asia-Pacific region (APAC), with a 28% increase driven by increased adoption of our AI-powered solutions. This APAC growth is particularly notable as it suggests our investments in localization and regional partnerships are bearing fruit. Our Q3 net margin expanded to 18.5%, a 250 basis point improvement compared to 16% in Q3 2022. This expansion wasn't solely attributable to increased revenue. We also implemented several key technical and operational initiatives that significantly contributed to enhanced profitability. One significant factor was the ongoing consolidation of our data center infrastructure. Our "Project Phoenix" initiative, aimed at migrating workloads to a more efficient and cost-effective hybrid cloud environment, has yielded substantial cost savings. Specifically, we saw a 12% reduction in our infrastructure operating expenses compared to the previous quarter. This project also allows us to dynamically allocate resources, further optimizing utilization and reducing waste. Our investment in automation technologies across our customer support and software development teams has driven significant efficiency gains. The implementation of AI-powered chatbots in customer support has reduced resolution times by 18% and lowered support costs by 15%. On the development front, automated testing and continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines have accelerated release cycles and reduced bug counts, leading to a more stable and cost-effective product development process. Our strategic shift towards higher-margin products and services also played a vital role. We’ve consciously focused on upselling and cross-selling our premium offerings, particularly within our cybersecurity suite. The adoption rate of our enhanced threat detection and response platform saw a 35% increase this quarter, contributing significantly to our higher average revenue per customer.

Finally, regarding utilization rates, in Q1 2020, our overall utilization rate stood at a robust 92%, reflecting strong demand across our portfolio. Specifically, 14nm utilization was at 95%, demonstrating continued maturity and optimization of that process, despite the increased capacity. We saw a slight dip in 10nm utilization to 88% in Q1, primarily due to a planned maintenance shutdown at our Fab 7 facility in Singapore and a temporary slowdown in orders from a major smartphone client undergoing a product refresh. However, we anticipate this will be a short-term blip. Looking ahead to Q2 2020, we are providing utilization rate guidance in the range of 90-93%. This reflects several factors. Firstly, we expect the 10nm utilization to rebound strongly to above 92% as the smartphone client's new product ramps up. Secondly, the additional 14nm capacity coming online towards the end of Q1 will begin to contribute meaningfully in Q2, supporting demand from the automotive and industrial sectors. We project 14nm utilization to remain above 93%. Finally, we are also anticipating a moderate increase in 7nm demand, although this is not directly related to the 14nm and 10nm capacity expansion, it does contribute to overall fab loading. We are therefore confident in our ability to maintain strong utilization rates.

I’ll now pass it over to Sarah to walk through the numbers in more detail.

Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Mark, and hello, everyone.

Let me break it down starting with utilization rates. As a reminder, between 2018 and 2019, we significantly expanded our wafer start capacity by 25% to support growing demand, particularly in high-performance computing and mobile applications. Building on this foundation, we are continuing our strategic capacity investments in 2020, adding another 25% capacity for both our 14nm and 10nm processes. This expansion is crucial for servicing our commitments to key customers and capitalizing on emerging opportunities in the AI and automotive sectors. Beyond Q2, our outlook for utilization rates remains positive, driven by several key trends. The ongoing global rollout of 5G infrastructure is generating significant demand for our 14nm and 10nm processes, particularly for base station equipment and networking chips. We are seeing strong orders from key telecom equipment providers. The adoption of AI across various industries, from cloud computing to autonomous vehicles, is fueling demand for high-performance processors and accelerators manufactured on our advanced nodes. The 10nm node is particularly well-suited for many AI applications. The automotive industry is undergoing a technological revolution, with increasing demand for advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), electric vehicles (EVs), and connected car technologies. These applications require sophisticated chips manufactured on our 14nm and 10nm processes. We've recently secured a multi-year agreement with a leading German automotive OEM, which will contribute significantly to our fab loading in the coming years. We are actively pursuing opportunities to diversify our customer base and expand our geographic presence. We are seeing increased demand from emerging markets, particularly in Southeast Asia and India. In response, we are strategically allocating capacity to serve these regions. To further optimize utilization rates and improve operational efficiency, we are implementing several key initiatives. We are investing heavily in advanced process control technologies to improve yield and reduce cycle times. This will enable us to maximize output from our existing capacity. We are implementing predictive maintenance programs to minimize downtime and prevent unplanned disruptions. This will help us maintain high utilization rates and ensure consistent delivery to our customers. We are continuously refining our capacity allocation models to ensure that we are matching supply with demand in the most efficient way possible. This includes dynamically adjusting capacity based on market trends and customer forecasts. We are closely aligning our technology roadmap with customer needs to ensure that we are developing the right processes to meet their future requirements. We anticipate that these initiatives, combined with the strong demand drivers we are seeing across our key markets, will enable us to sustain high utilization rates and deliver strong financial performance in the years to come.

Now, moving to our gross margin performance. As communicated in our Q2 2023 earnings call, our full-year expectation for gross margin remains unchanged at approximately 60%. This reflects our confidence in our ability to navigate the current macroeconomic environment and execute our strategic initiatives. However, Q3 presented a mixed bag, and understanding the drivers behind the quarterly results is crucial. While we are maintaining our full-year guidance, Q3 gross margin landed at 59.2%, a slight underperformance compared to our internal guidance of 60.5% projected last quarter. This 1.3 percentage point difference requires a more in-depth explanation. Several factors contributed to the observed variance, both positive and negative. A significant driver was a shift in revenue mix. While Q3 revenue saw a 15% increase year-over-year to $2.3 billion, the composition of that revenue differed from our projections. Specifically, our higher-margin SaaS offerings experienced slightly slower growth than anticipated, while our hardware sales, particularly in the enterprise infrastructure segment, exceeded expectations. Hardware, while still profitable, carries a lower gross margin, typically in the 45-50% range, compared to our SaaS offerings, which boast gross margins of 70-75%. This shift diluted the overall blended gross margin. For example, SaaS contributed 55% of revenue instead of the projected 58%. While supply chain disruptions have largely eased, we continue to experience elevated component costs, particularly for memory chips used in our high-performance computing servers. This impacted the cost of goods sold (COGS) for our hardware division, reducing the gross margin on those sales by approximately 2 percentage points compared to our Q2 experience. We are actively working with our suppliers to negotiate more favorable pricing and explore alternative component sourcing strategies, but these efforts will take time to fully materialize. To drive sales in the competitive small and medium-sized business (SMB) market, we implemented targeted promotional campaigns, particularly in the North American region. These promotions, which included discounted pricing on bundled software and hardware solutions, successfully boosted unit sales volume, but at the expense of short-term gross margin. The promotional activities accounted for an estimated 0.5 percentage point reduction in the overall Q3 gross margin. We believe this investment was strategically sound, as it allowed us to acquire new customers and increase market share in a key segment. The projected lifetime value of these acquired customers outweighs the short-term margin impact. The strengthening of the US dollar against the Euro and the Japanese Yen also had a slight negative impact on our reported gross margin. Because a significant portion of our manufacturing costs are denominated in these currencies, the stronger dollar increased our reported COGS when translated back into USD. This effect accounted for approximately 0.2 percentage points of the margin shortfall. We have hedging strategies in place to mitigate currency risk, but these strategies are not always perfectly effective in the short term. Our ongoing investment in automation within our manufacturing facilities, particularly in our Southeast Asian plants, is beginning to yield positive results. These initiatives, aimed at improving production efficiency and reducing labor costs, contributed positively to gross margin, offsetting some of the negative impacts mentioned above. We estimate that the automation initiatives added approximately 0.3 percentage points to the Q3 gross margin. We anticipate that these benefits will continue to grow as we further scale our automation efforts. Performance varied significantly by region. While North America faced higher promotional activity, Europe and Asia-Pacific (APAC) performed strongly, particularly in our cloud services offerings. APAC, driven by strong demand from the financial services sector, exceeded expectations in cloud adoption, contributing positively to the overall gross margin. However, the positive impact from Europe and APAC was not enough to fully offset the headwinds in North America and the impact of the revenue mix shift. Despite the slight underperformance in Q3, we remain confident in our ability to achieve our full-year gross margin target of approximately 60%. Several factors support this confidence. We anticipate that our SaaS growth will accelerate in Q4, driven by the launch of several new product features and increased marketing efforts. This shift back towards a higher proportion of SaaS revenue will help to improve our blended gross margin. We expect that component costs will continue to moderate in Q4 as supply chain disruptions ease further. This will reduce the pressure on our hardware gross margins. We are actively reviewing our pricing strategies across all product lines to ensure that we are capturing appropriate value for our products and services. This includes implementing more dynamic pricing models and reducing reliance on broad-based promotional discounts. We are continuing to invest in operational efficiencies across our entire organization, including manufacturing, supply chain, and customer support. These efforts will help to reduce costs and improve our overall profitability.

Lastly, I'd like to briefly touch on our sales guidance. Let's break down our revenue guidance for the remainder of 2019, focusing on the fourth quarter and providing a fuller picture for the full year. As previously announced, we are increasing our full-year 2019 revenue outlook by $1.5 billion to $71 billion. This reflects stronger-than-anticipated performance in several key areas, particularly within our Data-Centric businesses in the first half of the year. We maintain our expectation of flat to slightly up revenue growth for the full year for our Data-Centric Businesses. While the first half of the year saw robust growth driven by strong demand for our cloud solutions and advancements in AI, we anticipate a more moderate pace in the second half due to increasing macroeconomic headwinds and a degree of digestion following significant investments in cloud infrastructure by major hyperscalers. Specifically, we project Data-Centric revenue to land between $35.4 billion and $35.8 billion. Within DCG, the Cloud & Enterprise segment continues to be a significant growth driver. We anticipate this segment to achieve approximately $21.5 billion for the full year, reflecting a year-over-year increase of approximately 5%. This is fueled by the continued adoption of our next-generation Xeon Scalable processors and accelerating demand for workload-optimized solutions. We've seen particularly strong uptake in the financial services and healthcare sectors, where our secure and scalable platforms are enabling significant advancements in areas like algorithmic trading and personalized medicine. Performance in our Network and Edge area has been somewhat variable. While 5G infrastructure deployments are progressing, the pace is slower than initially anticipated. We now project revenue in this segment to be approximately $8 billion for the full year, a slight decrease of around 2% year-over-year. However, we are optimistic about the long-term potential of this segment as 5G adoption accelerates and edge computing solutions gain broader traction. We are investing heavily in software-defined networking (SDN) and network function virtualization (NFV) technologies to capitalize on this trend. The memory market remains highly cyclical. While average selling prices (ASPs) have stabilized somewhat in recent quarters, we anticipate full-year revenue in this segment to be approximately $5.8 billion, down approximately 5% year-over-year. This reflects the impact of lower ASPs earlier in the year and ongoing inventory adjustments within the channel. We are strategically shifting our focus towards higher-value memory solutions, such as 3D NAND and Optane Persistent Memory, to mitigate the impact of commodity price fluctuations. Our expectations for the PC-Centric business remain largely unchanged. We continue to anticipate revenue to be flat to slightly down for the full year. We project CCG revenue to land between $35.2 billion and $35.6 billion. We are seeing a stabilization of the traditional desktop PC market, offset by declines in the notebook segment due to component shortages. The desktop market continues to be a stable contributor, driven by demand from enterprise customers upgrading their aging infrastructure. We anticipate desktop revenue to be approximately $10 billion for the full year, roughly flat compared to the previous year. The notebook market has experienced some volatility due to component shortages, particularly in the display and memory sectors. We now project notebook revenue to be approximately $20 billion for the full year, down approximately 2% year-over-year. Our adjacent product lines, including Wi-Fi and Thunderbolt technologies, are performing well. We anticipate these products to generate approximately $5.4 billion in revenue for the full year, up approximately 3% year-over-year. This growth is driven by increasing demand for high-speed connectivity and peripherals. For the fourth quarter, we expect revenue to be approximately $19.2 billion, representing a 3% increase year-over-year and remaining flat sequentially. This reflects a combination of factors, including continued strength in our Data-Centric businesses and a seasonal uptick in PC demand. We project Data-Centric revenue to be up 6% to 8% year-over-year in Q4, driven by continued demand for our cloud solutions and a ramp-up in new product deployments. We anticipate revenue in this segment to be between $8.7 Billion and $8.9 billion. We expect the Cloud & Enterprise segment to continue its strong performance, with revenue up approximately 10% year-over-year in Q4. We are seeing particularly strong demand for our second-generation Xeon Scalable processors, which are now being widely adopted by cloud service providers and enterprise customers. We anticipate a more moderate pace of growth in the Network and Edge segment in Q4, with revenue up approximately 3% year-over-year. While 5G deployments are progressing, the timing of infrastructure investments remains uncertain. We expect the memory market to remain stable in Q4, with revenue roughly flat compared to the previous year. We are focused on managing our inventory levels and strategically shifting our product mix towards higher-value solutions. We expect the PC-Centric business to be flat to slightly down year-over-year in Q4. We anticipate revenue in this segment to be between $10.3 billion and $10.5 billion. This reflects a seasonal uptick in PC demand, offset by ongoing component shortages and increased competition.

Now, let me hand things over to David to talk about product and operational progress.

David Lee, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Sarah.

This was a busy quarter for our teams. On the innovation front, we made meaningful advances around our next-generation AI inference engine, Project Nightingale. This included the release of Nightingale v2, which is already demonstrating a 30% performance improvement compared to the previous version in internal benchmarks. Early customer feedback has been overwhelmingly positive, with several key clients reporting significant reductions in latency and improved accuracy in their AI-powered applications.

Also worth noting is our improvement in operating margin. A key contributor to this was our expansion into the Asia-Pacific region. Specifically, the Southeast Asia market has demonstrated remarkable growth, with Q3 revenue increasing by 28% year-over-year. This region benefits from lower labor costs and a rapidly growing customer base, contributing to higher operating margins compared to our more established markets in North America and Europe. While operating costs were projected to be 18% of sales, they came in at 16.5% showing efficiencies of scale.

And we’ve made foundational changes in how we approach sales forecasting, particularly on the fulfillment and logistics side. In North America, we continue to see strong demand, driven by robust economic growth and significant investments in cloud infrastructure. We are experiencing mixed results in Asia-Pacific. While China remains a large and important market, we are seeing signs of slowing economic growth and increased trade tensions. We are closely monitoring these developments and adjusting our strategy accordingly. We are seeing stronger growth in other parts of the region, such as India and Southeast Asia. The European market remains challenging, with ongoing political and economic uncertainty. We are focused on managing our costs and selectively investing in growth opportunities.

Let’s now open the floor for questions.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. On the EPS results, could you expand on what’s driving that strength?

Mark Thompson:
Certainly. Beyond the revenue growth and cost efficiencies that Sarah and I discussed, the ongoing consolidation of our data center infrastructure through "Project Phoenix" has been a major factor. The 12% reduction in infrastructure operating expenses has had a direct positive impact on our bottom line. Furthermore, the strategic shift towards higher-margin cybersecurity offerings is also contributing significantly to the EPS beat. We are seeing increased adoption of our premium security services, reflecting a growing demand for robust threat protection solutions. We expect these trends to continue, supporting further EPS growth in the coming quarters.

Analyst 2:
A follow-up on utilization rates. How confident are you that the 10nm utilization will rebound to above 92% in Q2, given the earlier slowdown?

Sarah Chen:
We have very high confidence in the Q2 rebound. Our visibility into our client's product roadmap is strong, and initial feedback on the new product launch has been very positive. However, as a prudent measure, we have identified alternative customers and applications that can absorb the 10nm capacity in the unlikely event of a further delay. Specifically, we are in discussions with several cloud computing providers who are interested in using our 10nm process for their AI accelerators. We also have the flexibility to shift some of the 10nm capacity to other advanced nodes if needed. While this would require some tooling adjustments, it is a viable option.

Analyst 3:
And for Project Nightingale, any update on commercialization plans?

David Lee:
Yes, we are on track for a broader commercial launch of Nightingale v2 in Q4. We are currently working closely with a select group of early access partners to refine the product and gather feedback. We anticipate strong demand for Nightingale v2 across a range of industries, including healthcare, finance, and retail, where AI-powered decision-making is becoming increasingly critical. We are also exploring strategic partnerships with leading AI platform providers to expand our reach and accelerate adoption.

Analyst 4:
Just a final one — on the sales forecast, is the improvement mostly driven by volume or pricing?

Sarah Chen:
It's a combination of both, but volume is the primary driver. While we have implemented some selective price increases on certain product lines, the majority of the revenue growth is attributable to increased unit sales, particularly in our cloud and enterprise segments. We are seeing strong demand for our latest generation Xeon Scalable processors, which are delivering significant performance and efficiency gains for our customers. We are also benefiting from the continued expansion of the cloud market, as more and more businesses migrate their workloads to the cloud.

Closing

Mark Thompson:
Thank you again for joining us today. We remain confident in our long-term growth story and are committed to disciplined execution. We appreciate your continued interest and support.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
